answer: Because the dawn calculation reruns each epoch, the cedar weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the ember settlement publishes the resulting shares. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 33% independent neighbours on the funding graph. A tight ring of 125 clones as a result holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 5 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
